title: Modal verbs in reporting
summary: Как ведут себя модальные глаголы в косвенной речи: will/can/may/shall сдвигаются в would/could/might/should, а would, could, might, should, ought to остаются; особый случай — must.
ru:
## Общий принцип
Если глагол вводящей части стоит в прошедшем (**said, told, asked, explained**), то модальные глаголы обычно «сдвигаются назад», как и обычные времена. Но не все: часть модальных уже выглядит как прошедшая форма или вообще не имеет формы прошедшего времени, поэтому остаётся без изменений.
> 'I **will** finish it by Monday.' → She said she **would** finish it by Monday. — Она сказала, что закончит к понедельнику.
> 'You **should** see a specialist.' → He said I **should** see a specialist. — Он сказал, что мне стоит показаться специалисту.

## Меняются: will, can, may, shall
- **will → would**: 'We'll announce the results soon.' → They said they **would** announce the results soon.
- **can → could**: 'I can't open the file.' → He complained that he **couldn't** open the file.
- **may → might** (возможность) или **could / might** (разрешение): 'It may rain later.' → She said it **might** rain later.
- **shall → would / should**: 'Shall I book a table?' → He asked if he **should** book a table. (предложение); 'I shall be there.' → He said he **would** be there. (формальное будущее).

## Не меняются: would, could, might, should, ought to
Эти формы уже «сдвинуты» (или не имеют прошедшей формы), поэтому в косвенной речи они остаются прежними. Так же ведут себя **had better, used to** и **needn't** (needn't можно также передать как **didn't need to / didn't have to**).
> 'You **ought to** apologise.' → She said I **ought to** apologise. — Она сказала, что мне следует извиниться.
> 'I **might** change my mind.' → He said he **might** change his mind. — Он сказал, что может передумать.
> 'You **had better** not be late.' → She warned me that I **had better** not be late.

## must: три разных случая
Здесь легко ошибиться, потому что **must** передаёт разные значения.
- **Обязанность** → **had to** (или **must**, если обязанность ещё в силе): 'You must submit the form today.' → He told us we **had to** submit the form that day.
- **Логический вывод** → **must** не меняется: 'He must be exhausted.' → I said he **must** be exhausted. Форму *had to* здесь не используют — она прочитается как обязанность: ~~I said he had to be exhausted~~.
- **Запрет (mustn't)** → **mustn't** остаётся или **wasn't / weren't allowed to**: 'You mustn't park here.' → He said we **mustn't** park there. / ...we **weren't allowed to** park there.

## Вопросы и просьбы
Вопросы с модальными вводятся через **asked + if/whether / вопросительное слово**, порядок слов прямой, а модальный сдвигается по тем же правилам:
> 'Can you send me the report?' → She asked if I **could** send her the report.
> 'Will you be joining us?' → He asked whether I **would** be joining them.
> 'When should we start?' → They asked when they **should** start.
На просьбу с *Could you...?* / *Would you...?* часто отвечают глаголом **asked + объект + to + инфинитив**: She **asked me to** send the report. Это нейтральнее и короче.

## Когда сдвиг не обязателен
Если вводящий глагол стоит в Present или Present Perfect, сдвига нет вообще: 'The tickets **will** be available from May.' → The agency says the tickets **will** be available from May. При вводящем глаголе в прошедшем модальный можно не сдвигать, если сказанное остаётся верным в момент пересказа: 'You **can** only pay by card.' → The cashier told me I **can** only pay by card (это правило действует и сейчас).

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~He said he will come.~~ → He said he **would** come. (при вводящем глаголе в прошедшем)
- ~~She asked if could I help.~~ → She asked if **I could** help.
- ~~I said he had to be tired.~~ → I said he **must** be tired. (вывод)
- ~~They said we should to leave.~~ → They said we **should** leave.
- ~~He said I mustn't to enter.~~ → He said I **mustn't** enter.
en:
## The basic idea
When the reporting verb is in the past (**said, told, asked, explained**), modal verbs normally shift back, like ordinary tenses. But some modals already look like past forms or have no past form, so they stay as they are.
> 'I **will** finish it by Monday.' → She said she **would** finish it by Monday.
> 'You **should** see a specialist.' → He said I **should** see a specialist.

## Modals that change: will, can, may, shall
- **will → would**: 'We'll announce the results soon.' → They said they **would** announce the results soon.
- **can → could**: 'I can't open the file.' → He complained that he **couldn't** open the file.
- **may → might** (possibility) or **could / might** (permission): 'It may rain later.' → She said it **might** rain later.
- **shall → would / should**: 'Shall I book a table?' → He asked if he **should** book a table (an offer); 'I shall be there.' → He said he **would** be there (formal future).

## Modals that stay: would, could, might, should, ought to
These are already 'shifted' or have no past form, so they do not change in reported speech. **had better, used to** and **needn't** behave in the same way (needn't can also become **didn't need to / didn't have to**).
> 'You **ought to** apologise.' → She said I **ought to** apologise.
> 'I **might** change my mind.' → He said he **might** change his mind.

## must: three different cases
**must** can express different meanings, and each is reported differently.
- **Obligation** → **had to** (or **must** if the obligation still exists): 'You must submit the form today.' → He told us we **had to** submit the form that day.
- **Deduction** → **must** stays: 'He must be exhausted.' → I said he **must** be exhausted. *had to* is not used here: it would sound like an obligation.
- **Prohibition (mustn't)** → **mustn't** stays, or **wasn't / weren't allowed to**: 'You mustn't park here.' → He said we **mustn't** park there.

## Questions and requests
Questions with modals are introduced by **asked + if/whether / a question word**, with normal word order, and the modal shifts as above:
> 'Can you send me the report?' → She asked if I **could** send her the report.
> 'When should we start?' → They asked when they **should** start.
A request with *Could you...?* / *Would you...?* is often reported with **asked + object + to + infinitive**: She **asked me to** send the report.

## When no shift is needed
After a present or present perfect reporting verb there is no shift at all: The agency says the tickets **will** be available from May. After a past reporting verb you may keep the modal unchanged if the statement is still true: The cashier told me I **can** only pay by card.

## Common mistakes
- ~~He said he will come.~~ → He said he **would** come.
- ~~She asked if could I help.~~ → She asked if **I could** help.
- ~~I said he had to be tired.~~ → I said he **must** be tired. (deduction)
- ~~They said we should to leave.~~ → They said we **should** leave.
structure:
## Сдвиг модальных глаголов
| Прямая речь | Косвенная речь | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| will | would | She said she **would** call. |
| can / can't | could / couldn't | He said he **couldn't** come. |
| may | might / could | They said it **might** snow. |
| shall (предложение) | should | He asked if he **should** wait. |
| shall (будущее) | would | I said I **would** be late. |
| must (обязанность) | had to / must | We were told we **had to** register. |
| must (вывод) | must | I thought she **must** be ill. |
| mustn't | mustn't / weren't allowed to | She said we **mustn't** talk. |
| would, could, might, should, ought to, had better, used to | без изменений | He said I **ought to** rest. |

## Вопросы
> asked + if / whether + подлежащее + модальный (сдвинутый) + глагол
> She asked **whether** we **could** start earlier.

> asked + вопросительное слово + подлежащее + модальный + глагол
> He asked **where** they **should** meet.

## Запросы и приказы без модального
> asked / told + объект + (not) to + инфинитив
> She **asked me to** wait. · He **told us not to** park here.

exercises.title: Сдвиг модальных глаголов
exercises.instruction: Допишите косвенную речь. Вводящий глагол стоит в прошедшем времени. Вставьте нужный модальный глагол.
exercises.example: 'I can swim.' → She said she **could** swim.

items.text: 'We will call you tomorrow.' → They promised they {{would}} call me the next day.
'I can't find my passport.' → Marco said he {{couldn't|could not}} find his passport.
'It may be a mistake.' → The editor said it {{might|could}} be a mistake.
'Shall I carry your bag?' → He asked if he {{should}} carry my bag.
'You should rest more.' → The doctor told me I {{should}} rest more.
'I won't tell anyone.' → She assured us that she {{wouldn't|would not}} tell anyone.
'You ought to read the contract.' → My lawyer said I {{ought to}} read the contract.
'I may leave early.' → Helen said she {{might|could}} leave early.

exercises.title: must: обязанность или вывод?
exercises.instruction: Вставьте **had to** или **must** (если возможны оба варианта, укажите оба).

items.text: 'You must wear a helmet on the site.' → The foreman said we {{had to|must}} wear a helmet on the site.
'She must be very proud of you.' → I told him she {{must}} be very proud of him.
'You must register before the deadline.' → The clerk told us we {{had to|must}} register before the deadline.
'They must be lost by now.' → I suspected that they {{must}} be lost by then.
'You mustn't open the box.' → She told me I {{mustn't|must not}} open the box.
'The results must be wrong.' → The scientist said the results {{must}} be wrong.

exercises.title: Выберите правильный вариант
exercises.instruction: Выберите вариант, который корректно передаёт прямую речь.

items.q: 'I will be back by noon.' → He said he ___ back by noon.
items.why: При вводящем глаголе в прошедшем will → would.

items.q: 'It must be a joke.' → I said it ___ a joke.
items.why: Логический вывод передаётся через must; had to означало бы обязанность.

items.q: 'Could you open the window?' → She asked me ___ the window.
items.why: Просьба удобно передаётся конструкцией asked + объект + to + инфинитив.

items.q: 'You mustn't touch anything.' → The guard said we ___ anything.
items.why: mustn't остаётся без изменений (допустимо и weren't allowed to touch).

items.q: 'When shall we meet?' → They asked when they ___ meet.
items.why: shall в вопросе о том, как поступить, превращается в should.

items.q: 'You had better call her.' → He told me I ___ call her.
items.why: had better не меняется в косвенной речи.

items.q: 'We can use the lab.' → She said we ___ use the lab.
items.why: can → could; после модального инфинитив без to.

options: She asked if could I help her.
She asked if I could help her.
She asked if I can to help her.
items.why: В косвенном вопросе прямой порядок слов: if I could help.

items.q: 'He must be tired.' (вывод) Какой вариант верный?
options: He said he had to be tired.
He said he must be tired.
He said he must to be tired.
items.why: Для вывода используется must, а не had to.

options: They said we should to wait.
They said we would should wait.
items.why: После should инфинитив без to; формы would should не существует.

options: The manager told that we had to stay.
The manager told us we had to stay.
The manager said us we had to stay.
items.why: tell требует объекта (told us), say — нет (said that).

options: She asked whether I would be joining them.
She asked whether would I be joining them.
She asked whether I will be joining them.
items.why: Прямой порядок слов и сдвиг will → would.

options: He warned me I mustn't be late.
He warned me I don't must be late.
He warned me I musn't being late.
items.why: mustn't остаётся без изменений, дальше идёт инфинитив без to.

exercises.title: Передайте слова косвенной речью
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложения в косвенной речи, начав так, как указано.

items.prompt: 'I can attend the meeting.' → Paula said ...
answers: Paula said she could attend the meeting.
Paula said that she could attend the meeting.

items.prompt: 'We will deliver the goods on Friday.' → The supplier promised ...
answers: The supplier promised they would deliver the goods on Friday.
The supplier promised that they would deliver the goods on Friday.
The supplier promised the goods would be delivered on Friday.
The supplier promised that the goods would be delivered on Friday.
The supplier promised they'd deliver the goods on Friday.
The supplier promised that they'd deliver the goods on Friday.
The supplier promised to deliver the goods on Friday.

items.prompt: 'Shall I turn the heating off?' → He asked ...
answers: He asked if he should turn the heating off.
He asked whether he should turn the heating off.
He asked if he should turn off the heating.
He asked whether he should turn off the heating.
He asked me if he should turn the heating off.
He asked me whether he should turn the heating off.
He asked me if he should turn off the heating.
He asked me whether he should turn off the heating.

items.prompt: 'You might want to check the figures.' → She suggested that I ...
answers: She suggested that I might want to check the figures.
She suggested that I should check the figures.
She suggested that I check the figures.

items.prompt: 'Can you give me a lift?' → She asked ...
answers: She asked if I could give her a lift.
She asked whether I could give her a lift.
She asked me to give her a lift.
She asked me if I could give her a lift.
She asked me whether I could give her a lift.

items.prompt: 'You must be joking!' → I told him he ...
answers: I told him he must be joking.
I told him that he must be joking.

exercises.title: Перефразирование
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, заменив прямую речь косвенной. Начало дано.

items.prompt: 'It may be too late to apply.' → The advisor warned us that it ...
answers: The advisor warned us that it might be too late to apply.
The advisor warned us that it could be too late to apply.

items.prompt: 'You needn't bring any documents.' → The receptionist said that we ...
answers: The receptionist said that we needn't bring any documents.
The receptionist said that we need not bring any documents.
The receptionist said that we didn't need to bring any documents.
The receptionist said that we did not need to bring any documents.
The receptionist said that we didn't have to bring any documents.
The receptionist said that we did not have to bring any documents.

items.prompt: 'Will you be able to start on Monday?' → The director asked me whether ...
answers: The director asked me whether I would be able to start on Monday.
The director asked me whether I'd be able to start on Monday.

items.prompt: 'We must leave before the storm hits.' → The captain said that they ...
answers: The captain said that they had to leave before the storm hit.
The captain said that they had to leave before the storm hits.
The captain said that they must leave before the storm hit.
The captain said that they must leave before the storm hits.

items.prompt: 'I couldn't hear a word.' → She complained that she ...
answers: She complained that she couldn't hear a word.
She complained that she could not hear a word.

items.prompt: 'Should we reschedule the conference?' → They wondered whether ...
answers: They wondered whether they should reschedule the conference.
They wondered if they should reschedule the conference.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте полными предложениями, используя косвенную речь с модальными глаголами.

items.prompt: Передайте совет, который вам недавно дал друг или коллега (should / ought to / might).
items.sample: My colleague said I should take a few days off before the deadline.
My landlord promised he would repair the heating before winter.

items.prompt: Передайте запрет или правило, которое вы услышали (mustn't / weren't allowed to).
items.sample: The receptionist said we mustn't use the lift during the fire drill.

items.prompt: Передайте вопрос, который вам задали (asked if ... could / should).
items.sample: A tourist asked me if I could recommend a good restaurant nearby.
